title: 2019 EJU Session 1 — Mathematics (Course 2)
source: Examination for Japanese University Admission for International Students, 2019 Session 1 (JASSO). Official English question paper; answers verified against the official answer key and re-derived by solving.
note: The exam has four large questions (大問 I-IV). In Course 2, large questions I and II each contain two independent sub-questions (問1, 問2); these are stored as separate entries, giving six questions. Parts I-Q1 and I-Q2 are shared with Course 1. Answer-letters follow the official scheme and reset at the start of each large question. The official answer key OCR interleaves the Course 1 and Course 2 columns; every box here was both re-solved and matched to the Course 2 column. For II-Q1 (vectors) only the first box (A) is cleanly OCR-readable in the key; the remaining boxes B-L are determined by rigorous solving (numerically verified), as noted in the report.

questions.subtopic: Reading signs of coefficients from a parabola graph, then minimizing a^2-8b-8c under graph constraints

en.prompt:
**[I] Q1 — Quadratic functions.** *(For $\boxed{A}$–$\boxed{K}$ choose the correct symbol/number from the list $⓪$–$⑨$ below.)*

Consider the quadratic function $y=ax^2+bx+c$ whose graph is the parabola shown: it opens downward, passes through the point $(1,0)$ on the $x$-axis, and has its vertex to the right of the $y$-axis with positive $y$-intercept.

(1) Then $a,b,c$ satisfy: (i) $a\,\boxed{A}\,0,\ b\,\boxed{B}\,0,\ c\,\boxed{C}\,0$; (ii) $a+b+c\,\boxed{D}\,0$; (iii) $a-b+c\,\boxed{E}\,0$; (iv) $4a+2b+c\,\boxed{F}\,0$; (v) $b^2-4ac\,\boxed{G}\,0$.

(2) Under conditions (i) and (ii), minimize $a^2-8b-8c$. We find $a=\boxed{H}$. Writing $y=ax^2+bx+c$ in terms of $b$, $y=\boxed{H}\,x^2+bx-b+\boxed{I}$. The range of $b$ is $\boxed{J}<b<\boxed{K}$.

Choices: $⓪\ 0\quad ①\ 1\quad ②\ 2\quad ③\ 3\quad ④\ 4\quad ⑤\ -2\quad ⑥\ -4\quad ⑦\ >\quad ⑧\ =\quad ⑨\ <$

ja.prompt:
**[Ⅰ] 問1 — 二次関数** *（$\boxed{A}$〜$\boxed{K}$ は下の選択肢 $⓪$〜$⑨$ から選べ。）*

二次関数 $y=ax^2+bx+c$ のグラフが図のような放物線であるとする：上に凸で，$x$ 軸上の点 $(1,0)$ を通り，頂点は $y$ 軸の右にあり，$y$ 切片は正である。

(1) このとき $a,b,c$ は次を満たす：(i) $a\,\boxed{A}\,0,\ b\,\boxed{B}\,0,\ c\,\boxed{C}\,0$；(ii) $a+b+c\,\boxed{D}\,0$；(iii) $a-b+c\,\boxed{E}\,0$；(iv) $4a+2b+c\,\boxed{F}\,0$；(v) $b^2-4ac\,\boxed{G}\,0$。

(2) 条件 (i),(ii) のもとで $a^2-8b-8c$ を最小にする。$a=\boxed{H}$ となる。$y=ax^2+bx+c$ を $b$ で表すと $y=\boxed{H}\,x^2+bx-b+\boxed{I}$。$b$ の範囲は $\boxed{J}<b<\boxed{K}$。

選択肢：$⓪\ 0\quad ①\ 1\quad ②\ 2\quad ③\ 3\quad ④\ 4\quad ⑤\ -2\quad ⑥\ -4\quad ⑦\ >\quad ⑧\ =\quad ⑨\ <$

explanation.en:
The parabola opens downward, so $a<0$ ($\boxed{A}=⑨\,<$). Its $y$-intercept is positive, so $c>0$ ($\boxed{C}=⑦\,>$). The vertex is at $x=-b/(2a)>0$; since $a<0$ this forces $b>0$ ($\boxed{B}=⑦\,>$).
(ii) The graph passes through $(1,0)$, so $a+b+c=0$ ($\boxed{D}=⑧\,=$).
(iii) $a-b+c$ is the value at $x=-1$, which lies left of the left root, so it is negative: $a-b+c<0$ ($\boxed{E}=⑨\,<$).
(iv) $4a+2b+c$ is the value at $x=2$, beyond the right root, hence negative ($\boxed{F}=⑨\,<$).
(v) Two distinct real roots give $b^2-4ac>0$ ($\boxed{G}=⑦\,>$).
(2) From (ii) $b+c=-a$, so $a^2-8b-8c=a^2-8(b+c)=a^2+8a=(a+4)^2-16$, minimized at $a=-4$ ($\boxed{H}=⑥\,-4$). Then $c=-a-b=4-b$, so $y=-4x^2+bx+(4-b)=-4x^2+bx-b+4$ ($\boxed{I}=④\,4$). The conditions $b>0$ and $c=4-b>0$ give $0<b<4$ ($\boxed{J}=⓪,\ \boxed{K}=④$).
explanation.ja:
放物線は上に凸なので $a<0$（$\boxed{A}=⑨$）。$y$ 切片が正なので $c>0$（$\boxed{C}=⑦$）。頂点 $x=-b/(2a)>0$ かつ $a<0$ より $b>0$（$\boxed{B}=⑦$）。
(ii) $(1,0)$ を通るので $a+b+c=0$（$\boxed{D}=⑧$）。
(iii) $a-b+c$ は $x=-1$ での値で，左の解より左にあり負：$a-b+c<0$（$\boxed{E}=⑨$）。
(iv) $4a+2b+c$ は $x=2$ での値で，右の解より右にあり負（$\boxed{F}=⑨$）。
(v) 相異なる2実解より $b^2-4ac>0$（$\boxed{G}=⑦$）。
(2) (ii) より $b+c=-a$ なので $a^2-8b-8c=a^2+8a=(a+4)^2-16$，$a=-4$ で最小（$\boxed{H}=⑥$）。$c=4-b$ より $y=-4x^2+bx-b+4$（$\boxed{I}=④$）。$b>0$ かつ $c=4-b>0$ より $0<b<4$（$\boxed{J}=⓪,\ \boxed{K}=④$）。

questions.subtopic: Biased die (6 twice as likely): single-roll probability, then two- and three-roll comparisons of complementary events

en.prompt:
**[I] Q2 — Probability.** Consider die-X: for each of $1$ through $5$ the probability is the same, but the probability of $6$ is twice that of any other number.

(1) Let $p$ be the probability a particular number $1$–$5$ comes up. Then $P(6)=\boxed{L}\,p$. Since the total probability is $\boxed{M}$, we get $p=\dfrac{\boxed{N}}{\boxed{O}}$.

(2) Die-X is rolled twice. Let $A$ be the event that both rolls show $1$–$5$, and $B$ the event that $6$ appears at least once. Then $P(A)=\dfrac{\boxed{PQ}}{\boxed{RS}}$ and $P(B)=\dfrac{\boxed{TU}}{\boxed{VW}}$. Hence $\boxed{X}$, choosing from: $⓪$ $P(A)<P(B)$ and the difference is $\ge\tfrac1{36}$; $①$ $P(A)<P(B)$ and the difference is $<\tfrac1{36}$; $②$ $P(A)=P(B)$; $③$ $P(A)>P(B)$ and the difference is $\ge\tfrac1{36}$; $④$ $P(A)>P(B)$ and the difference is $<\tfrac1{36}$.

(3) Die-X is rolled three times. Let $C$ be the event that all three show $1$–$5$, and $D$ the event that $6$ appears at least once. Then $\boxed{Y}$, choosing from: $⓪$ $P(C)<P(D)$ and $P(D)\ge 2P(C)$; $①$ $P(C)<P(D)$ and $P(D)<2P(C)$; $②$ $P(C)=P(D)$; $③$ $P(C)>P(D)$ and $P(C)\ge 2P(D)$; $④$ $P(C)>P(D)$ and $P(C)<2P(D)$.

ja.prompt:
**[Ⅰ] 問2 — 確率** さいころ X を考える：$1$ から $5$ の出る確率は等しいが，$6$ の出る確率は他のどの目の $2$ 倍である。

(1) $1$〜$5$ のある目が出る確率を $p$ とすると $P(6)=\boxed{L}\,p$。全確率は $\boxed{M}$ なので $p=\dfrac{\boxed{N}}{\boxed{O}}$。

(2) X を $2$ 回振る。両方とも $1$〜$5$ である事象を $A$，$6$ が少なくとも $1$ 回出る事象を $B$ とすると $P(A)=\dfrac{\boxed{PQ}}{\boxed{RS}}$，$P(B)=\dfrac{\boxed{TU}}{\boxed{VW}}$。よって $\boxed{X}$。選択肢：$⓪$ $P(A)<P(B)$ で差が $\tfrac1{36}$ 以上；$①$ $P(A)<P(B)$ で差が $\tfrac1{36}$ 未満；$②$ $P(A)=P(B)$；$③$ $P(A)>P(B)$ で差が $\tfrac1{36}$ 以上；$④$ $P(A)>P(B)$ で差が $\tfrac1{36}$ 未満。

(3) X を $3$ 回振る。すべて $1$〜$5$ である事象を $C$，$6$ が少なくとも $1$ 回出る事象を $D$ とすると $\boxed{Y}$。選択肢：$⓪$ $P(C)<P(D)$ で $P(D)\ge 2P(C)$；$①$ $P(C)<P(D)$ で $P(D)<2P(C)$；$②$ $P(C)=P(D)$；$③$ $P(C)>P(D)$ で $P(C)\ge 2P(D)$；$④$ $P(C)>P(D)$ で $P(C)<2P(D)$。

answer.en: $P(6)=2p$, total $=1$, $p=\tfrac17$; $P(A)=\tfrac{25}{49}$, $P(B)=\tfrac{24}{49}$ (so $④$); three rolls give $①$.  Boxes: L=2, M=1, NO=17, PQRS=2549, TUVW=2449, X=4, Y=1.

explanation.en:
(1) The six probabilities are $p,p,p,p,p,2p$, so $P(6)=2p$ ($\boxed{L}=2$). Their sum is the total probability $1$ ($\boxed{M}=1$): $5p+2p=7p=1\Rightarrow p=\tfrac17$ ($\boxed{NO}=17$).
(2) $P(\text{one roll in }1\text{–}5)=5p=\tfrac57$. $P(A)=(\tfrac57)^2=\tfrac{25}{49}$. $P(B)=1-P(A)=\tfrac{24}{49}$. Thus $P(A)>P(B)$ with difference $\tfrac{1}{49}<\tfrac1{36}$, so $\boxed{X}=④$.
(3) $P(C)=(\tfrac57)^3=\tfrac{125}{343}$, $P(D)=1-\tfrac{125}{343}=\tfrac{218}{343}$. Here $P(C)<P(D)$; and $2P(C)=\tfrac{250}{343}>\tfrac{218}{343}=P(D)$, so $P(D)<2P(C)$, giving $\boxed{Y}=①$.
explanation.ja:
(1) $6$ 個の確率は $p,p,p,p,p,2p$ で $P(6)=2p$（$\boxed{L}=2$）。総和は全確率 $1$（$\boxed{M}=1$）：$7p=1\Rightarrow p=\tfrac17$（$\boxed{NO}=17$）。
(2) $1$ 回で $1$〜$5$ の確率は $5p=\tfrac57$。$P(A)=(\tfrac57)^2=\tfrac{25}{49}$，$P(B)=1-P(A)=\tfrac{24}{49}$。$P(A)>P(B)$ で差 $\tfrac1{49}<\tfrac1{36}$，よって $\boxed{X}=④$。
(3) $P(C)=(\tfrac57)^3=\tfrac{125}{343}$，$P(D)=\tfrac{218}{343}$。$P(C)<P(D)$ かつ $2P(C)=\tfrac{250}{343}>P(D)$，すなわち $P(D)<2P(C)$ なので $\boxed{Y}=①$。

questions.subtopic: Tetrahedron inscribed in a sphere with a diametral edge: position vectors of midpoints, centroid, and collinearity

en.prompt:
**[II] Q1 — Vectors.** *(For $\boxed{A},\boxed{B},\boxed{D},\boxed{E},\boxed{G}$ choose the correct vector from the list $⓪$–$⑨$ below; for the other boxes enter a number.)*

A sphere of radius $2$ is centered at $O$, and a tetrahedron $ABCD$ has all four vertices on the sphere. Let $AB=BC=CA=2$, and let side $BD$ be a diameter of the sphere. Put $\vec a=\overrightarrow{OA},\ \vec b=\overrightarrow{OB},\ \vec c=\overrightarrow{OC}$.

(1) Let $M,N$ be the midpoints of $DA,BC$. Then $\overrightarrow{DA}=\boxed{A}$ and $\overrightarrow{MN}=\dfrac{\boxed{B}}{\boxed{C}}+\boxed{D}$.

(2) Let $P$ be the midpoint of $MN$ and $G$ the centroid of triangle $BCD$. Then $\overrightarrow{OP}=\dfrac{\boxed{E}}{\boxed{F}}$, $\overrightarrow{OG}=\dfrac{\boxed{G}}{\boxed{H}}$, and $\overrightarrow{PG}=\dfrac{\boxed{I}}{\boxed{J}}\,\overrightarrow{AP}$. Since $\overrightarrow{AG}=\dfrac{\boxed{K}}{\boxed{L}}\,\overrightarrow{AP}$, the three points $A,P,G$ are collinear.

Choices: $⓪\ \vec a\quad ①\ \vec b\quad ②\ \vec c\quad ③\ \vec a-\vec b\quad ④\ \vec b-\vec c\quad ⑤\ \vec c-\vec a\quad ⑥\ \vec a+\vec b\quad ⑦\ \vec b+\vec c\quad ⑧\ \vec c+\vec a\quad ⑨\ \vec a+\vec b+\vec c$

ja.prompt:
**[Ⅱ] 問1 — ベクトル** *（$\boxed{A},\boxed{B},\boxed{D},\boxed{E},\boxed{G}$ は下の選択肢 $⓪$〜$⑨$ から選び，他の空欄には数を入れよ。）*

中心 $O$，半径 $2$ の球面に，四面体 $ABCD$ の $4$ 頂点がすべて乗っている。$AB=BC=CA=2$ とし，辺 $BD$ は球の直径とする。$\vec a=\overrightarrow{OA},\ \vec b=\overrightarrow{OB},\ \vec c=\overrightarrow{OC}$ とおく。

(1) $M,N$ を $DA,BC$ の中点とすると $\overrightarrow{DA}=\boxed{A}$，$\overrightarrow{MN}=\dfrac{\boxed{B}}{\boxed{C}}+\boxed{D}$。

(2) $P$ を $MN$ の中点，$G$ を三角形 $BCD$ の重心とすると $\overrightarrow{OP}=\dfrac{\boxed{E}}{\boxed{F}}$，$\overrightarrow{OG}=\dfrac{\boxed{G}}{\boxed{H}}$，$\overrightarrow{PG}=\dfrac{\boxed{I}}{\boxed{J}}\,\overrightarrow{AP}$。$\overrightarrow{AG}=\dfrac{\boxed{K}}{\boxed{L}}\,\overrightarrow{AP}$ なので，$3$ 点 $A,P,G$ は一直線上にある。

選択肢：$⓪\ \vec a\quad ①\ \vec b\quad ②\ \vec c\quad ③\ \vec a-\vec b\quad ④\ \vec b-\vec c\quad ⑤\ \vec c-\vec a\quad ⑥\ \vec a+\vec b\quad ⑦\ \vec b+\vec c\quad ⑧\ \vec c+\vec a\quad ⑨\ \vec a+\vec b+\vec c$

answer.en: $\overrightarrow{DA}=\vec a+\vec b\,(⑥)$; $\overrightarrow{MN}=\tfrac{\vec c-\vec a}{2}+\vec b$ ($⑤/2+①$); $\overrightarrow{OP}=\tfrac{\vec c+\vec a}{4}$ ($⑧/4$); $\overrightarrow{OG}=\tfrac{\vec c}{3}$ ($②/3$); $\overrightarrow{PG}=\tfrac13\overrightarrow{AP}$; $\overrightarrow{AG}=\tfrac43\overrightarrow{AP}$.  Boxes: A=6, B=5, C=2, D=1, E=8, F=4, G=2, H=3, I=1, J=3, K=4, L=3.
answer.ja: $\overrightarrow{DA}=\vec a+\vec b\,(⑥)$；$\overrightarrow{MN}=\tfrac{\vec c-\vec a}{2}+\vec b$（$⑤/2+①$）；$\overrightarrow{OP}=\tfrac{\vec c+\vec a}{4}$（$⑧/4$）；$\overrightarrow{OG}=\tfrac{\vec c}{3}$（$②/3$）；$\overrightarrow{PG}=\tfrac13\overrightarrow{AP}$；$\overrightarrow{AG}=\tfrac43\overrightarrow{AP}$。 解答：A=6, B=5, C=2, D=1, E=8, F=4, G=2, H=3, I=1, J=3, K=4, L=3。

explanation.en:
Since $BD$ is a diameter and $O$ is the center, $O$ is the midpoint of $BD$, so $\overrightarrow{OD}=-\vec b$. With $|\vec a|=|\vec b|=|\vec c|=2$ and $AB=BC=CA=2$, each pairwise dot product is $\vec a\cdot\vec b=\vec b\cdot\vec c=\vec c\cdot\vec a=2$.
(1) $\overrightarrow{DA}=\overrightarrow{OA}-\overrightarrow{OD}=\vec a-(-\vec b)=\vec a+\vec b$ ($\boxed{A}=⑥$). $\overrightarrow{OM}=\tfrac12(\overrightarrow{OD}+\overrightarrow{OA})=\tfrac12(\vec a-\vec b)$ and $\overrightarrow{ON}=\tfrac12(\vec b+\vec c)$, so $\overrightarrow{MN}=\overrightarrow{ON}-\overrightarrow{OM}=\tfrac12(\vec c-\vec a)+\vec b$ ($\boxed{B}=⑤,\ \boxed{C}=2,\ \boxed{D}=①$).
(2) $\overrightarrow{OP}=\tfrac12(\overrightarrow{OM}+\overrightarrow{ON})=\tfrac14(\vec a+\vec c)=\tfrac{\vec c+\vec a}{4}$ ($\boxed{E}=⑧,\ \boxed{F}=4$). $\overrightarrow{OG}=\tfrac13(\overrightarrow{OB}+\overrightarrow{OC}+\overrightarrow{OD})=\tfrac13(\vec b+\vec c-\vec b)=\tfrac{\vec c}{3}$ ($\boxed{G}=②,\ \boxed{H}=3$). Now $\overrightarrow{AP}=\overrightarrow{OP}-\vec a=-\tfrac34\vec a+\tfrac14\vec c$ and $\overrightarrow{PG}=\overrightarrow{OG}-\overrightarrow{OP}=-\tfrac14\vec a+\tfrac1{12}\vec c=\tfrac13\overrightarrow{AP}$ ($\boxed{I}=1,\ \boxed{J}=3$). Hence $\overrightarrow{AG}=\overrightarrow{AP}+\overrightarrow{PG}=\tfrac43\overrightarrow{AP}$ ($\boxed{K}=4,\ \boxed{L}=3$), so $A,P,G$ are collinear.
explanation.ja:
$BD$ は直径で $O$ が中心なので $O$ は $BD$ の中点，よって $\overrightarrow{OD}=-\vec b$。$|\vec a|=|\vec b|=|\vec c|=2$ かつ $AB=BC=CA=2$ より $\vec a\cdot\vec b=\vec b\cdot\vec c=\vec c\cdot\vec a=2$。
(1) $\overrightarrow{DA}=\vec a-(-\vec b)=\vec a+\vec b$（$\boxed{A}=⑥$）。$\overrightarrow{OM}=\tfrac12(\vec a-\vec b),\ \overrightarrow{ON}=\tfrac12(\vec b+\vec c)$ より $\overrightarrow{MN}=\tfrac12(\vec c-\vec a)+\vec b$（$\boxed{B}=⑤,\ \boxed{C}=2,\ \boxed{D}=①$）。
(2) $\overrightarrow{OP}=\tfrac14(\vec a+\vec c)=\tfrac{\vec c+\vec a}{4}$（$\boxed{E}=⑧,\ \boxed{F}=4$）。$\overrightarrow{OG}=\tfrac13(\vec b+\vec c-\vec b)=\tfrac{\vec c}{3}$（$\boxed{G}=②,\ \boxed{H}=3$）。$\overrightarrow{AP}=-\tfrac34\vec a+\tfrac14\vec c$，$\overrightarrow{PG}=-\tfrac14\vec a+\tfrac1{12}\vec c=\tfrac13\overrightarrow{AP}$（$\boxed{I}=1,\ \boxed{J}=3$）。よって $\overrightarrow{AG}=\tfrac43\overrightarrow{AP}$（$\boxed{K}=4,\ \boxed{L}=3$）で $A,P,G$ は一直線上。

questions.subtopic: Triangle on the complex plane from a quadratic relation among side ratios; modulus/argument and area

en.prompt:
**[II] Q2 — Complex plane.** Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ represent three distinct points $A,B,C$ on the complex plane, satisfying
$$(\gamma-\alpha)^2+(\gamma-\alpha)(\beta-\alpha)+(\beta-\alpha)^2=0,\qquad |\beta-2\alpha+\gamma|=3.$$
Find the area of triangle $ABC$ (take $-\pi<\arg<\pi$).

From the first relation, $\dfrac{\gamma-\alpha}{\beta-\alpha}=\dfrac{-\boxed{M}\pm\sqrt{\boxed{N}}\,i}{\boxed{O}}$, so $\left|\dfrac{\gamma-\alpha}{\beta-\alpha}\right|=\boxed{P}$ and $\arg\dfrac{\gamma-\alpha}{\beta-\alpha}=\pm\dfrac{\boxed{Q}}{\boxed{R}}\pi$.

Also $\beta-2\alpha+\gamma=(\beta-\alpha)\cdot\dfrac{\boxed{S}\pm\sqrt{\boxed{T}}\,i}{\boxed{U}}$, so from the second relation $|\beta-\alpha|=\boxed{V}$.

Therefore the area of triangle $ABC$ is $\dfrac{\boxed{W}\sqrt{\boxed{X}}}{\boxed{Y}}$.

ja.prompt:
**[Ⅱ] 問2 — 複素数平面** 複素数平面上の相異なる $3$ 点 $A,B,C$ を表す $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ が次を満たす：
$$(\gamma-\alpha)^2+(\gamma-\alpha)(\beta-\alpha)+(\beta-\alpha)^2=0,\qquad |\beta-2\alpha+\gamma|=3。$$
三角形 $ABC$ の面積を求めよ（$-\pi<\arg<\pi$ とする）。

第1式より $\dfrac{\gamma-\alpha}{\beta-\alpha}=\dfrac{-\boxed{M}\pm\sqrt{\boxed{N}}\,i}{\boxed{O}}$ なので，$\left|\dfrac{\gamma-\alpha}{\beta-\alpha}\right|=\boxed{P}$，$\arg\dfrac{\gamma-\alpha}{\beta-\alpha}=\pm\dfrac{\boxed{Q}}{\boxed{R}}\pi$。

また $\beta-2\alpha+\gamma=(\beta-\alpha)\cdot\dfrac{\boxed{S}\pm\sqrt{\boxed{T}}\,i}{\boxed{U}}$ なので，第2式より $|\beta-\alpha|=\boxed{V}$。

よって三角形 $ABC$ の面積は $\dfrac{\boxed{W}\sqrt{\boxed{X}}}{\boxed{Y}}$。

answer.en: $\tfrac{\gamma-\alpha}{\beta-\alpha}=\tfrac{-1\pm\sqrt3 i}{2}$, modulus $1$, argument $\pm\tfrac23\pi$; $\beta-2\alpha+\gamma=(\beta-\alpha)\tfrac{1\pm\sqrt3 i}{2}$ so $|\beta-\alpha|=3$; area $=\tfrac{9\sqrt3}{4}$.  Boxes: M=1, N=3, O=2, P=1, QR=23, S=1, T=3, U=2, V=3, W=9, X=3, Y=4.
answer.ja: $\tfrac{\gamma-\alpha}{\beta-\alpha}=\tfrac{-1\pm\sqrt3 i}{2}$，絶対値 $1$，偏角 $\pm\tfrac23\pi$；$\beta-2\alpha+\gamma=(\beta-\alpha)\tfrac{1\pm\sqrt3 i}{2}$ より $|\beta-\alpha|=3$；面積 $=\tfrac{9\sqrt3}{4}$。 解答：M=1, N=3, O=2, P=1, QR=23, S=1, T=3, U=2, V=3, W=9, X=3, Y=4。

explanation.en:
Let $w=\dfrac{\gamma-\alpha}{\beta-\alpha}$. Dividing the first relation by $(\beta-\alpha)^2$ gives $w^2+w+1=0$, so $w=\dfrac{-1\pm\sqrt3\,i}{2}$ ($\boxed{M}=1,\boxed{N}=3,\boxed{O}=2$). Then $|w|=1$ ($\boxed{P}=1$) and $\arg w=\pm\tfrac{2}{3}\pi$ ($\boxed{QR}=23$).
Next $\beta-2\alpha+\gamma=(\beta-\alpha)+(\gamma-\alpha)=(\beta-\alpha)(1+w)$, and $1+w=1+\dfrac{-1\pm\sqrt3 i}{2}=\dfrac{1\pm\sqrt3\,i}{2}$ ($\boxed{S}=1,\boxed{T}=3,\boxed{U}=2$), which has modulus $1$. So $|\beta-2\alpha+\gamma|=|\beta-\alpha|\cdot1=3$, giving $|\beta-\alpha|=3$ ($\boxed{V}=3$).
Finally $|\gamma-\alpha|=|w||\beta-\alpha|=3$, and the angle at $A$ is $\arg w=\tfrac23\pi$ (interior $\tfrac23\pi$, $\sin=\tfrac{\sqrt3}2$), so the area $=\tfrac12|\beta-\alpha||\gamma-\alpha|\sin\tfrac{2\pi}{3}=\tfrac12\cdot3\cdot3\cdot\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=\tfrac{9\sqrt3}{4}$ ($\boxed{W}=9,\boxed{X}=3,\boxed{Y}=4$).
explanation.ja:
$w=\dfrac{\gamma-\alpha}{\beta-\alpha}$ とおく。第1式を $(\beta-\alpha)^2$ で割ると $w^2+w+1=0$，よって $w=\dfrac{-1\pm\sqrt3\,i}{2}$（$\boxed{M}=1,\boxed{N}=3,\boxed{O}=2$）。$|w|=1$（$\boxed{P}=1$），$\arg w=\pm\tfrac23\pi$（$\boxed{QR}=23$）。
$\beta-2\alpha+\gamma=(\beta-\alpha)(1+w)$，$1+w=\dfrac{1\pm\sqrt3\,i}{2}$（$\boxed{S}=1,\boxed{T}=3,\boxed{U}=2$）で絶対値 $1$。よって $|\beta-2\alpha+\gamma|=|\beta-\alpha|=3$，$|\beta-\alpha|=3$（$\boxed{V}=3$）。
$|\gamma-\alpha|=|w||\beta-\alpha|=3$，$A$ での角は $\tfrac23\pi$（$\sin=\tfrac{\sqrt3}2$）なので 面積 $=\tfrac12\cdot3\cdot3\cdot\tfrac{\sqrt3}2=\tfrac{9\sqrt3}{4}$（$\boxed{W}=9,\boxed{X}=3,\boxed{Y}=4$）。

questions.subtopic: Feet of perpendiculars from points at angles theta and 3theta on the unit circle; maximize the gap via a cubic in cos theta

en.prompt:
**[III] — Unit circle.** On a coordinate plane let $C$ be the unit circle centered at $O$. For $0\le\theta\le\pi$, let $P,Q$ be the points where the radii at angles $\theta$ and $3\theta$ from the positive $x$-axis meet $C$. Let $A,B$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $P,Q$ to the $x$-axis, and let $\ell$ be the length of $AB$.

(1) When $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, $\ell=\dfrac{\boxed{A}}{\boxed{B}}$.

(2) Set $\cos\theta=t$. Then $\ell=\boxed{C}\,t^{\boxed{D}}-\boxed{E}\,t$. With $g(t)=\boxed{C}\,t^{\boxed{D}}-\boxed{E}\,t$, we have $g'(t)=\boxed{F}\big(\boxed{G}\,t^{\boxed{H}}-1\big)$. questions.subtopic: Inequality x-1>=log x, area between a line and a logarithm, then minimizing the area over k and its limit

en.prompt:
**[IV] — Logarithm, area, limit.** Here $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

(1) Let $f(x)=x-1-\log x$. Then $f'(x)=\boxed{A}-\dfrac{\boxed{B}}{x}$. The minimum is at $x=\boxed{C}$ with value $\boxed{D}$, which gives $x-1\ge\log x$.

(2) *(For $\boxed{G}$ choose from the list $⓪$–$③$ below; for the others enter a number.)* Let $k>0$ and $n$ a positive integer. Let $S$ be the area bounded by $y=\dfrac{x}{k}-1$, $x=n$, $x=n+1$ and $y=\log\dfrac{x}{k}$. Using (1),
$$S=\left[\dfrac{x^{\boxed{E}}}{\boxed{F}\,k}-x-\boxed{G}+x\log k\right]_{n}^{n+1}=\dfrac{\boxed{H}\,n+1}{\boxed{I}\,k}+\log k-(n+\boxed{J})\log(n+\boxed{K})+n\log n.$$

(3) Fix $n$ and vary $k>0$; let $a_n$ be the minimum of $S$. Then $\dfrac{dS}{dk}=\dfrac{\boxed{L}\,k-(\boxed{M}\,n+1)}{\boxed{N}\,k^{2}}$, so $S$ is minimized at $k=n+\dfrac{\boxed{O}}{\boxed{P}}$, and
$$a_n=\boxed{Q}-\log\!\left[\left(\boxed{R}+\dfrac{\boxed{S}}{n}\right)^{n}\cdot\dfrac{\boxed{T}\,n+\boxed{U}}{\boxed{V}\,n+1}\right],\qquad \lim_{n\to\infty}a_n=\boxed{W}.$$

Choices for $\boxed{G}$: $⓪\ x(\log x+1)\quad ①\ x(\log x-1)\quad ②\ \dfrac{\log x+1}{x}\quad ③\ \dfrac{\log x-1}{x}$

(1) $f'(x)=1-\tfrac1x$ ($\boxed{A}=1,\boxed{B}=1$); $f'(x)=0$ at $x=1$ ($\boxed{C}=1$), where $f$ has its minimum $f(1)=0$ ($\boxed{D}=0$). Hence $x-1-\log x\ge0$, i.e. $x-1\ge\log x$.

An antiderivative is $\tfrac{x^2}{2k}-x-x(\log x-1)+x\log k$, using $\int\log x\,dx=x(\log x-1)$ ($\boxed{G}=①$, $\boxed{E}=2,\boxed{F}=2$).
